## Goal

A single, well-tested way for the application to learn a request's network origin and country, so request-rate controls and security records attribute attempts to the right visitor behind a reverse proxy.

## Context

Several code paths each derive this information on their own today. Behind a reverse proxy, whether such a value can be trusted depends on how the proxy is configured, and the deployment this project is moving to has not been verified yet. The independent review rates the resulting uncertainty a launch condition for the self-hosted deployment. Specifics are in the owner's private tracker.

## Scope

- One module that resolves the request origin and country, with an explicit, configured trust model and a documented default for each environment.
- Every current call site uses it; none derives the value itself.
- Correct, validated handling of both address families, including the shortened notation, with a documented masking rule for anything stored.
- Defined behaviour when the value is absent, so distinct visitors are not merged.
- `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md` states exactly what the proxy must do, and `docs/SECURITY.md` records the contract.

## Out of scope

- Changing the rate-limit policy itself (SC-021).
- Changing form behaviour beyond the swap to the new module (SC-020).
- Proxy configuration on a server.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests prove the resolved value cannot be influenced by request content when the deployment follows the documented contract.
- [ ] Tests cover the absent value, both address families and the shortened notation.
- [ ] No call site derives the value on its own any more (shown by a search in the PR).
- [ ] Behaviour on the current host is unchanged.
- [ ] Independent review approves.

## Required tests

- Unit tests for the module, table-driven over the documented cases.
- Tests for each call site.
- All standard checks.

## Dependencies

- SC-003
